text.p: Following its decision on Tuesday morning to elect Jose Maria Gil-Robles as its president for the next two and a half years, the European Parliament has elected 14 new vice-presidents to assist the new leader.

Scottish radical MEP Winnie Ewing complained that the reshuffle, which was only achieved after three irritable rounds of voting, means that six of the European Union's 15 member states - Austria, Belgium, Finland, Ireland, the Netherlands, and Sweden -- will not be represented on the Parliament's top decision making body, the political bureau.
Ten of the 14 incoming vice-presidents have already held their posts since June 1994 under outgoing president Klaus Haensch, a German Socialist.
Socialists Paraskevas Avgerinos (Greece), Renzo Imbeni (Italy), David Martin (UK), Nicole Pery (France) and Josep Verde I Alea (Spain) were all reelected.
So were Christian Democrats Georgios Anastassopoulos (Greece), Nicole Fontaine (France), Ursula Schleicher (Germany) and Antonio Capucho (Portugal).
Capucho was the Liberal group's only vice-president until he defected to the Christian Democrat European People's Party (EPP) last November.
Antoni Gutierrez Diaz, a Spaniard from the United Left (GUE), also retained his post.

Four new vice-presidents joined the incumbents: Danish Liberal Bertel Haarder, German Socialist Magdalene Hoff, Portuguese Socialist Luis Marinho and Italian Union for Europe (UPE) member Guido Podesta.
The reshuffle gives Parliament's largest political formation, the 214-member Socialist group, a total of seven vice-presidents.
The 181-strong EPP, Parliament's second largest group, now has four vice-presidents in addition to the new Spanish president.
Of the smaller groups, the UPE (57 members), Liberals (43) and GUE (33) each have one new vice-president.
This leaves the 28-member Green group, the 20-member Radical Alliance, the 18-member Independent Europe of Nations group and the 32 independent MEPs out in the cold.
Parliament also elected two of its five new quaestors (Parliament's top administrators) on Tuesday. They are British Socialist Richard Balfe and Portuguese United Left deputy Sergio Ribeiro.
Christian Democrats Otto Bardong (Germany) and Vincenzo Viola (Italy), and Irish Union for Europe deputy Mark Killilea were expected to be elected late on Tuesday night.
